content.prompt:
Decide whether these functions are odd, even, or neither.

You may need to use $|-x|=|x|$ and $|x-y|=|y-x|$. Check your answers using DESMOS.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f(-x)&=|-x|+1\\&=|x|+1\\&=f(x).\end{align*}$$
Therefore $f$ is even. Its graph is symmetric about the $y$-axis.

$$\begin{align*}f(1)&=|1|+1=2,\\f(-1)&=|-1|-1=0.\end{align*}$$
Since $f(-1)\ne f(1)$ and $f(-1)\ne-f(1)$, $f$ is neither even nor odd. Its graph has neither $y$-axis symmetry nor origin symmetry.

$$\begin{align*}f(-x)&=(-x)|-x|\\&=-x|x|\\&=-f(x).\end{align*}$$
Therefore $f$ is odd. Its graph is symmetric about the origin.

$$\begin{align*}f(-x)&=|(-x)^3+(-x)|\\&=|-x^3-x|\\&=|-(x^3+x)|\\&=|x^3+x|\\&=f(x).\end{align*}$$
Therefore $f$ is even. Its graph is symmetric about the $y$-axis.

For $x\ge0$, $|x|-x=0$, so the function is undefined. For $x<0$,
$$\begin{align*}f(x)&=\frac{x}{-x-x}\\&=\frac{x}{-2x}\\&=-\frac12.\end{align*}$$
The domain is $(-\infty,0)$, which is not symmetric about zero, so $f$ is neither even nor odd. Its graph is the horizontal ray $y=-\tfrac12$ for $x<0$, with neither required symmetry.

$$\begin{align*}f(-x)&=|-x-1|+|-x+1|\\&=|-(x+1)|+|-(x-1)|\\&=|x+1|+|x-1|\\&=f(x).\end{align*}$$
Therefore $f$ is even. Its graph is symmetric about the $y$-axis.

answer.worked:
Case 1:
$$\begin{aligned}x-5&=2x-6\\x&=1\end{aligned}$$
Case 2:
$$\begin{aligned}-(x-5)&=2x-6\\-x+5&=2x-6\\11&=3x\\x&=\frac{11}{3}\end{aligned}$$
Check in the original equation:
For $x=1$, LHS $=|1-5|=4$, while RHS $=2(1)-6=-4$. Reject $x=1$.
For $x=\frac{11}{3}$,
$$\begin{aligned}\left|\frac{11}{3}-5\right|&=\frac43\\2\left(\frac{11}{3}\right)-6&=\frac43\end{aligned}$$
Therefore $x=\frac{11}{3}$.

Case 1:
$$\begin{aligned}2x+1&=x\\x&=-1\end{aligned}$$
Case 2:
$$\begin{aligned}-(2x+1)&=x\\-2x-1&=x\\-1&=3x\\x&=-\frac13\end{aligned}$$
Check in the original equation:
For $x=-1$,
$$\begin{aligned}|2(-1)+1|&=1\\\text{RHS}&=-1\end{aligned}$$
Reject $x=-1$.
For $x=-\frac13$,
$$\begin{aligned}\left|2\left(-\frac13\right)+1\right|&=\frac13\\\text{RHS}&=-\frac13\end{aligned}$$
Reject $x=-\frac13$. Neither candidate satisfies the original equation, so there is no solution.

Case 1:
$$\begin{aligned}1-3x&=2x+4\\-3&=5x\\x&=-\frac35\end{aligned}$$
Case 2:
$$\begin{aligned}-(1-3x)&=2x+4\\-1+3x&=2x+4\\x&=5\end{aligned}$$
Check in the original equation:
For $x=-\frac35$,
$$\begin{aligned}\left|1-3\left(-\frac35\right)\right|&=\frac{14}{5}\\2\left(-\frac35\right)+4&=\frac{14}{5}\end{aligned}$$
For $x=5$,
$$\begin{aligned}|1-3(5)|&=14\\2(5)+4&=14\end{aligned}$$
Both candidates are valid. Therefore $x=-\frac35$ or $x=5$.

When there are variables on both sides, sometimes the algebra introduces an extra solution.
Always verify your solutions by substituting back into the original.

4 = x

Right branch:
−(x + 3) = 2x − 1
−x − 3 = 2x − 1
−2 = 3x
x = −2/3

Checking x = 4:
|4 + 3| = 2(4) − 1
7 = 7 ✓

Checking x = −2/3:
|−2/3 + 3| = 2(−2/3) − 1
7/3 = −7/3 ✗

Only x = 4 is a solution.
